page: Amazon Web Services r8idn.96xlarge is a high-capacity memory-optimized server configuration based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The platform operates on the x86_64 architecture using Intel processors operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. Hardware provisioning includes 192 physical cores yielding 384 dedicated vCPUs with two threads per core. System memory is scaled to 3072.0 GB, establishing a 1:8 core-to-memory ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Data throughput and local processing capabilities are augmented by 22,800 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD instance storage, enabling high-speed read and write operations directly adjacent to the compute cores. The network subsystem delivers a baseline bandwidth of 600 Gbps with dedicated EBS optimization. The configuration includes zero discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

By combining extreme memory density with extensive local NVMe storage capacity and high networking throughput, the instance facilitates substantial workload consolidation. The hardware profile is engineered to maintain low latency across data-intensive tasks without off-instance storage bottlenecks. Primary target workloads include enterprise in-memory database engines, large-scale distributed memory caches, real-time streaming analytics, and high-throughput data transformation pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8idn.96xlarge is a high-density, memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and x86_64 Intel processors running at 3.9 GHz. Designed for memory-centric and data-intensive requirements, the configuration integrates 22,800 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD instance storage and 600 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system contains no hardware accelerators or GPUs. This combination of vast memory density, ultra-high network throughput, and rapid local non-volatile storage provides significant infrastructure consolidation for enterprise environments. The instance is structured specifically to support demanding operational footprints such as large in-memory databases, high-capacity distributed caching systems, extract-transform-load (ETL) processing engines, and real-time big data analytics pipelines.
